text:
marcos: Quick scan of Q1 incident corpus — two high-frequency clusters popped out: 1) scheduler thrash where many small health-check failures + aggressive scaling cause request storms, and 2) memory fragmentation on long-lived inference workers that eventually OOM and restart. Sharing a short summary and proposed follow-ups.

trina: Interesting. For scheduler thrash, do we see a specific health-check path triggering it (liveness vs readiness)?

gopal: Mostly readiness probes; readiness flips caused a rapid churn in the endpoint list, LB started routing to half-warmed workers. Autoscaler then misread CPU as low and scaled down, then scale-up created pressure again.

mira: For memory fragmentation, we saw slow growth of heap gaps on RTX nodes running older runtime build. Not classic leak, more fragmentation + long-running token cache.

marcos: Good detail. Two quick tactical proposals: (A) add a short cooldown window and probe-spread for readiness, plus jittered retries; (B) schedule a periodic in-place defrag job and lower long-lived cache retention for tenants with infrequent traffic.

ops-bot: Metric note: incident 1808121111 had 27 readiness flips in 10m; median probe jitter was 5ms. Recommendation: set probe jitter 50-250ms and readiness-grace 10s.

trina: I can take the probe/jitter change and update the readiness docs + canary rollout. Owner: trina. ETA: 2026-04-07.

gopal: I'll run an experiment to add a small cold-start buffer in the LB so warmed instances get higher initial weight for 30s after start. Owner: gopal. ETA: 2026-04-12.

mira: I'll own the defrag cadence experiment and a config flag to reduce cache retention per-tenant. Owner: mira. ETA: 2026-04-20.

marcos: Action list for tracking (reply with :thumbsup: to accept):
- trina: readiness probe jitter + cooldown rollout (ETA 2026-04-07)
- gopal: LB warm-weight buffer experiment (ETA 2026-04-12)
- mira: periodic defrag + tenant cache retention flag (ETA 2026-04-20)
- ops-bot / infra: add pattern alert "scheduler-thrash" when endpoint churn >20 in 10m AND >2 scale events in 15m (ETA infra: 2026-04-03)

trina: +1 :thumbsup: will schedule canary.

gopal: +1. I'll post experiment plan to #eng-runtime.

mira: +1. Will include perf baseline and expected CPU impact.

marcos: I'll capture these items in the patterns tracker and add a short SQL query used to find the clusters:```sql
-- get candidate pattern clusters by root cause tag
SELECT root_cause, COUNT(*) as cnt, ARRAY_AGG(incident_id) as ids
FROM incidents
WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' AND created_at < '2026-04-01'
AND closed = true
GROUP BY root_cause
ORDER BY cnt DESC;
```

gopal: Can you also split by "runtime_version" so we can see if fragmentation correlates with old builds?

marcos: Done in tracker sheet. Added runtime_version and deployment_type filters.

ops-bot: Reminder set: follow-up sync on 2026-04-15 09:00 PT.

trina: Can we include a small success metric for the probe change? e.g., readiness flips per deploy drop >50% in canary cluster.

mira: For defrag, success metric: reduce memory-related restarts by 80% for flagged tenants in 30 days.

marcos: Sounds good. If anyone wants to break tasks out into smaller tickets, do it and link to the tracker row ID 42.

gopal: Will do and tag infra ownership.
